editorial:
You follow Dani and her boyfriend Christian as they join friends on a trip to a remote Swedish village for a rare summer festival. The endless daylight feels dreamy at first, but the cheerful locals hide strange customs that slowly pull the group into danger. Dani is grieving, so the trip also becomes a test of her relationship and trust.

Florence Pugh gives a powerful performance, and the bright, open setting makes the horror feel fresh. The film looks gorgeous in daylight, which makes the violence hit harder. The costumes, music, and rituals build a world that feels both beautiful and wrong. The pacing is slow, so you need patience, and some scenes are very disturbing. If you enjoy folk horror and emotional stories, this is worth your time. It is not for everyone, but it sticks with you.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Dani is crowned May Queen after the cult kills most of her friends. Christian is trapped inside a bear suit and burned alive in a temple as part of the ritual. Dani watches, smiles through tears, and finally seems to find a twisted sense of belonging with the community. The movie ends with her choosing the cult over her old life.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves folk horror, slow-burn dread, and character-driven stories.
